Accepted risk. Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp would block Stripe's cross-origin frames and scripts, breaking checkout. REVISIT if the Stripe frame dependency is ever removed, or adopt credentialless once browser support is uniform.
Scanner artifact. Flags that ZAP's own outbound requests omit Sec-Fetch-Dest; it is a request header set by browsers, not something the server controls.

Environment-induced, not a product defect. /checkout returns 500 in CI because STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is deliberately absent from the DAST job; production has it configured. The 500 is Next.js's production error page, which does not include a stack trace. REVISIT if this ever fires on a route that does not require live Stripe credentials.

Accepted known weakness, NOT a false positive. This rule id covers three faults at once; the no-fallback and wildcard variants were FIXED (form-action + frame-ancestors added, img-src https: removed). What remains is script-src 'unsafe-inline', which genuinely weakens XSS defence. Removing it requires nonce-based CSP generated in middleware and threaded through Next's inline bootstrap scripts — a real change with real breakage risk, not a config tweak. Because ZAP cannot ignore one variant of an id, tests/unit/csp.test.ts asserts the other two properties deterministically so this ignore does not silently drop that coverage. Formally accepted with compensating controls in docs/COMPLIANCE.md AR-1 (dated 2026-07-19); the key control is tests/unit/no-xss-sinks.test.ts, which fails the build if any HTML/JS execution sink is introduced. REVISIT when that guard fails or nonce/SRI CSP lands; delete this line then.
